title: 5 Cardigan restaurants you can try before a night hunting ghosts at a historic castle
excerpt: Planning a ghost hunt at Cardigan Castle? Discover five top nearby restaurants, from Welsh and British favourites to Italian, Indian and seasonal local cuisine.
content:
With centuries of history and tales of ghostly encounters, Cardigan Castle is the perfect setting for a night of paranormal investigation.

The castle has been home to two manifestations – a lady in white known as Ladi Wen could be seen walking the parapets in the 1860s, and a lady in black, believed to be the ghost of Arabella Davies, was seen during the Second World War.

Volunteers and staff have also reported hearing voices and noises coming from the room where the Escape Game Room is, as in 1897, the room’s occupant – 18-year-old George Davies – accidentally shot himself whilst there.

But before you go hunting for spirits, you might want to fuel up at one of Cardigan’s top-rated restaurants—all within easy walking distance of the castle.

Here are five of the best places to eat before an evening of spooky fun.

Yr Hen Printworks

Located in Carrier’s Lane in a converted chapel and printworks, Yr Hen Printworks serves seasonal small plates with global influences.

The restaurant has a 4.7 rating on Tripadvisor, with diners praising its flavours and relaxed atmosphere.

One reviewer said: "What a fantastic restaurant to have in the heart of Cardigan.

"Every dish was absolutely delicious, and the service was outstanding."

The Copper Pot

This family-run restaurant on Pendre offers classic British and Welsh comfort food, including steaks, burgers and mixed grills.

The Copper Pot also caters for vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free diets and has a 4.8 Tripadvisor rating.

"Excellent servers and atmosphere," one diner said. "Food was lovely and able to accommodate preferences."

Mannucci’s Italian Restaurant

Mannucci’s champions traditional Italian dishes using locally sourced ingredients. (Image: Mannucci’s)

Just a short walk from the castle, Mannucci’s serves traditional Italian dishes in a cosy, Tuscan-inspired setting.

The glass-walled ground floor and atmospheric upstairs dining room add to the experience.

It holds a 4.6 rating on Tripadvisor.

"Fantastic authentic Italian restaurant serving delicious food with great service and a very friendly atmosphere," one reviewer said.

Abdul’s Tandoori

For those craving spice, Abdul’s in Quay Street offers Indian, Bangladeshi and Pakistani cuisine.

The menu includes curries, biryanis, tandoori dishes and more, with vegetarian, vegan, halal and gluten-free options available.

It is rated 4.4 on Tripadvisor.

"Excellent food and service," one diner said. "Huge choice on the menu and taste of fresh, quality ingredients. Really good."

1176 at Cardigan Castle

1176 is set within the walls of Cardigan Castle. (Image: Google Street View)

Located within the castle grounds, 1176 serves seasonal Welsh dishes made from local ingredients.

The restaurant overlooks the River Teifi, making it an ideal spot for a late lunch before the evening’s ghostly activities.

It has a 4.3 rating on Tripadvisor, with one reviewer saying: "Wonderful food, definitely recommend the Sunday lunch."
